hook.line: Ask anyone in Bogotá where to get off the bus and you will hear streets and numbers, never a stop name. Tomás needs the phrase that goes with them.
hook.es: Me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.

examples.es: Me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.
El accidente fue a la altura de la iglesia.
examples.en: The accident happened level with the church.

examples.es: El café queda a la altura de la carrera séptima.
examples.en: The café is level with Carrera Séptima.

examples.es: Siga derecho y gire a la altura del semáforo.
examples.en: Keep going straight and turn at the traffic light (to a stranger, formal).

examples.es:
¿Dónde te bajas?
A la altura de la calle 26.
examples.en:
Where do you get off? (to a friend)
Around 26th Street.

examples.es: Mi casa queda a la altura de la iglesia.
examples.en: My house is level with the church.

rule:
To say where along a street something is, use *a la altura de* + a street, a number or a landmark. It means "around", "level with", "at about that point". It is looser than *en*: *en la calle 72* names the street, *a la altura de la calle 72* says you are near that point on the road.

It is not about height here, so never translate *altura* as "height".

*De + el* becomes *del*: *a la altura del semáforo*. Feminine places keep *de la*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a prepositional phrase of position. Figuratively, *estar a la altura* means "to rise to the occasion", which you will meet later.

readAndPick.es: Me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.
options: I get on around 72nd Street.
I get off around 72nd Street.
I get off 72 streets away.

readAndPick.es: El accidente fue a la altura de la iglesia.
options: The accident happened level with the church.
The accident will be inside the church.
The accident was as tall as the church.

readAndPick.es: El café queda a la altura de la carrera séptima.
options: The café closed on Carrera Séptima.
The café is on the top floor of Carrera Séptima.
The café is level with Carrera Séptima.

readAndPick.es: Siga derecho y gire a la altura del semáforo.
options: Keep straight and turn before the traffic light.
Keep straight and turn level with the traffic light.
Keep straight and turn after the traffic light.

readAndPick.es: Mi casa queda a la altura de la iglesia.
options: My house is as tall as the church.
My house is inside the church.
My house is level with the church along the street.

readAndPick.es: Vale se baja a la altura de la calle 26.
options: Vale gets off around 26th Street.
I get off around 26th Street.
You get off around 26th Street.

options: He gets off around 72nd Street.
They got off around 72nd Street.
They get off around 72nd Street.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de la* or *del*: Mi casa queda a la altura ___ iglesia. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Mi casa queda a la altura de la iglesia.
yourTurn.why: *Iglesia* is feminine, so *de la* stays two words.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de la* or *del*: Gire a la altura ___ semáforo. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Gire a la altura del semáforo.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I get off by 72nd Street.
yourTurn.answer: Me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.
accept: Yo me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.
yourTurn.why: *A la altura de* gives the rough point along the street.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The accident happened level with the church.
yourTurn.answer: El accidente fue a la altura de la iglesia.
yourTurn.why: The same phrase works for where an event happened.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a stranger (formal) to keep going straight and turn at the traffic light.
yourTurn.answer: Siga derecho y gire a la altura del semáforo.
yourTurn.why: Formal commands use the *usted* form, and *del* joins *de* and *el*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about Vale: *Me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.*
yourTurn.answer: Vale se baja a la altura de la calle 72.
accept: Ella se baja a la altura de la calle 72.
yourTurn.why: The verb changes to *se baja*, the phrase stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about them, in the past: *Me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.*
yourTurn.answer: Se bajaron a la altura de la calle 72.
yourTurn.why: The past plural is *se bajaron*, and the phrase stays the same.

pitfalls.wrong: Me bajo en la altura de la calle 72.
pitfalls.right: Me bajo a la altura de la calle 72.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase starts with *a*, not *en*.

pitfalls.wrong: Gire a la altura de el semáforo.
pitfalls.right: Gire a la altura del semáforo.

pitfalls.wrong: Mi casa queda a la altura la iglesia.
pitfalls.right: Mi casa queda a la altura de la iglesia.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Keep the *de*, which English hides inside "level with".

personal: Say where you get off, or where your favourite café is, using *a la altura de*: *Mi café favorito queda a la altura de…*
